title: HeyGen CEO Joshua Xu: How AI Lets Enterprises Produce Video 10× Faster on Ultra-Low Budgets
summary: Traditional enterprise video is slow and expensive: script, cast, locations, shoot, post, multi-language localization, possible reshoots — weeks to months, and astronomical for large productions. That blocks scaled video output.
author: Unique Research
html:
Unique Research · Insight / Interview digest · October 10, 2024 · Guest: Joshua Xu, Co-founder & CEO, HeyGen · Source interview: Unite.AI (Antoine Tardif); Unique Research compiled highlights

Traditional enterprise video is slow and expensive: script, cast, locations, shoot, post, multi-language localization, possible reshoots — weeks to months, and astronomical for large productions. That blocks scaled video output.

HeyGen’s AI video platform aims to break the bottleneck: studio-grade video in minutes, low-cost localization and personalization — no expensive cameras, crews, or actors. Provide a script; generate video for marketing, communications, sales, and employee training.

Core tech: advanced AI dubbing and lip-sync that can translate video into 175 languages and dialects while keeping the original speaker’s natural voice and emotion, with fluent target-language lip motion.

Traction: ARR from $1M → $35M+ in one year; profitable since Q2 2023. June this year: $60M Series A led by Benchmark at $500M+ valuation. Leadership adds: Dave King (ex-Asana CMO) as Chief Business Officer; Rong Yan (ex-HubSpot VP Eng) as CTO; Lavanya Poreddy (Match Group / Meta) as Head of Trust & Safety. 40,000+ paying customers spanning European manufacturers, SMBs, international nonprofits, and Fortune 500 — including McDonald’s “Sweet Connection” campaign and Salesforce partner launch work.

Q&A highlights

1. Why found HeyGen in 2020 — and the original vision?
Before HeyGen, Xu worked on Snap’s ads team integrating AI into Snapchat, then the AI-augmented camera team. In 2018 AI was not yet mainstream, but the team was exploring immature tech for image and video — and he saw computers could already create high-quality, highly realistic video. New mobile platforms (Instagram, Snapchat, TikTok) changed how creators shoot — but barriers remained: camera presence, time/resources to record, high production cost. HeyGen’s bet: the camera can be replaced. If you replace the camera, you remove barriers to visual storytelling.

2. Early challenges — ethics, trust, and growth?
Consumers were new to GenAI and questioned ethics. HeyGen’s policies and product strictly forbid unauthorized content; abuse is taken seriously. Safeguards include advanced user verification with live-video consent, dynamic spoken passwords, and fast human review of all avatar verifications — no known abuse since those protocols. Trust & safety is core; the company works industry-wide on tools and best practices against misinformation and AI misuse.

3. How does AI enable 10× video creation with less overhead?
Video editing itself is not that expensive — standing up a production team is. In a video-first world, enterprises want video engagement but stall on cost and complexity. HeyGen offers pro-grade generation plus TTS AI avatars that can dub from scratch — no studio, cast, or special skills. Without crews, gear, temperamental talent, reshoots, and long post, users make video ~10× faster — saving time/money and enabling scale that hits the P&L.

4. 175+ languages with natural lip-sync and voice?
TTS turns user text into audio; the team focuses on raising generation quality so people escape traditional cameras and expand what content production can be. (CN source answer is brief on the localization pipeline — no invented technical detail.)

5. Which industries adopt most among 40,000+ paid customers?
Especially enterprise marketing teams; video localization is a clear growth vector. Customers create, localize, and personalize without paying for a full production team.

6. McDonald’s and Weather Channel / UNDP outcomes?
McDonald’s “Sweet Connection”: grandchildren recorded messages in grandparents’ native languages via HeyGen translation — a proof of AI’s reach and inclusivity. UNDP “Weather Kids” with WMO and The Weather Channel: children as meteorologists deliver a 2050 climate forecast powered by HeyGen — part of UNDP’s push for climate awareness and action.

7. Where does AI video tech go next — and HeyGen’s position?
If people can easily make engaging video, they make more of it — and every enterprise wants more video output. HeyGen’s vision: personalized video with full-body avatars for all customers.

8. AI’s role in digital storytelling over five years?
Possibilities are open-ended. People already combine footage with AI editing tools. Continuing on GenAI can push performance far enough that streaming audiences experience GenAI-created work too.

9. Will AI video disrupt film?
HeyGen focuses on enterprise custom video, but believes compelling high-quality content is possible without a mobile camera. In creative arts, AI will remake film — not HeyGen’s core — yet easy localization via GenAI that cuts reshoot economics is an exciting adjacent vision.

10. How does the $60M Series A shape plans?
Already profitable since Q2 2023, so the round is mainly about world-class advisors/investors to scale — accelerate the product roadmap and grow GTM teams in Los Angeles, San Francisco, Palo Alto, and Toronto.

— END —
